title: Benchmarking fastINFLECT against consensus metaclustering
code: library(fastINFLECT) library(FlowSOM) load(system.file("extdata", "Levine32sample.Rdata", package = "fastINFLECT"))  # fastINFLECT: one call scores every k and recommends one. inflect_res <- INFLECT(dataset, set.i = 5:25, multicore = FALSE, zeroes.in = FALSE) # Original INFLECT pattern: one FlowSOMQC-style score per k, using dip.test() # inside every cluster-marker cell. The benchmark estimates this cost from sampled # original cells because a full old-engine run is intentionally slow. ml <- iteration.metacluster(dataset, set.i = 5:25, multicore = FALSE) legacy_qc <- lapply(5:25, function(k) {   FlowSOMQC(dataset, ml[[as.character(k)]], zeroes.in = FALSE, verbose = FALSE) }) codes <- dataset$map$codes  # (a) Convenience pattern: one metaClustering_consensus() call per k. Each call #     runs a fresh ConsensusClusterPlus up to maxK = k, so work is repeated. for (k in 5:25) mc_k <- metaClustering_consensus(codes, k = k, seed = 42)  # (b) Amortized: a single ConsensusClusterPlus run to maxK yields every k at once #     (this is what (a) slices internally). The fairest consensus baseline. ccp <- ConsensusClusterPlus::ConsensusClusterPlus(t(codes), maxK = 25, seed = 42,                                                   reps = 100, pItem = 0.9,                                                   pFeature = 1, clusterAlg = "hc",                                                   distance = "euclidean",                                                   plot = NULL, verbose = FALSE) # ... score ccp[[k]]$consensusClass for each k ...

title: Benchmarking fastINFLECT against consensus metaclustering
text: Time scan k = 5:25 (21 values) obtain quality score every k. consensus variants produce identical partitions; cost differs. original-INFLECT bar estimate 168 sampled original dip.test() cluster-marker cells; cache records sampling standard error, estimate excludes small metaclustering curve-fit overhead. Wall-clock scan score k = 5:25. fastINFLECT evaluates every distinct SOM-node subtree reuses across k. Original INFLECT estimated sampled original dip.test cells. single ConsensusClusterPlus run plus QC scoring fair consensus baseline; calling metaClustering_consensus() per k repeats work 21 times. fastINFLECT scans whole range 1.4 s. original INFLECT loop estimated 340.2 s (SE 25.3 s) (252× slower). fair consensus baseline — one ConsensusClusterPlus run — takes 62.9 s (47× slower), common per-k convenience pattern takes 677.9 s (502× slower). fastINFLECT cheapest one also returns recommended k.

code: sel <- cache$selection guides <- sel[is.finite(sel$k), ]  ggplot(cache$comparison_df, aes(x = k, y = unimodality, colour = method)) +   geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +   geom_point(size = 1.7) +   geom_vline(data = guides,              aes(xintercept = k, linetype = method),              colour = "grey30", show.legend = TRUE) +   scale_colour_manual(values = c("fastINFLECT (hierarchical cut)" = "#2E8B57",                                  "FlowSOM consensus" = "#E07B39"),                       name = "scan method") +   scale_linetype_manual(values = c(inflection = "dotted", kneedle = "dashed",                                     threshold = "longdash"),                         name = "fastINFLECT recommends k =",                         labels = paste0(guides$method, " (", round(guides$k), ")")) +   scale_x_continuous(breaks = cache$k_range) +   labs(x = "number of metaclusters (k)", y = "unimodal (cluster, marker) pairs (%)",        title = "Cluster quality by k") +   theme_bw(base_size = 11) +   theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) sel <- cache$selection uni_at <- function(k) {   d <- cache$comparison_df   d <- d[d$method == "fastINFLECT (hierarchical cut)", ]   hit <- d$unimodality[match(round(k), d$k)]   if (length(hit) == 0 || is.na(hit)) NA_real_ else round(hit, 1) } tbl <- data.frame(   Criterion = sel$method,   `Recommended k` = ifelse(is.na(sel$k), "—", as.character(round(sel$k))),   `Unimodality (%)` = vapply(sel$k, uni_at, numeric(1)),   check.names = FALSE ) knitr::kable(tbl, align = c("l", "r", "r"))

code: knee <- cache$inflect$lfunction$knee  # For fixed-k methods, report their best unimodality across the sweep # (the k that maximises unimodality — their theoretical optimum if the user chose perfectly) best_k <- function(method_name) {   d <- subset(cache$comparison_df, method == method_name)   d[which.max(d$unimodality), ] } best_consensus <- best_k("FlowSOM consensus") best_hclust    <- best_k("Hierarchical (ward.D2)")  # fastINFLECT score at its knee inflect_at_knee <- subset(cache$inflect$collection.U, i == knee)  tbl <- rbind(   data.frame(     Method            = "FlowSOM consensus",     `k selection`     = "manual",     `Best k in sweep` = best_consensus$k,     `Unimodality (%)` = round(best_consensus$unimodality, 1),     stringsAsFactors  = FALSE, check.names = FALSE   ),   data.frame(     Method            = "Hierarchical (ward.D2)",     `k selection`     = "manual",     `Best k in sweep` = best_hclust$k,     `Unimodality (%)` = round(best_hclust$unimodality, 1),     stringsAsFactors  = FALSE, check.names = FALSE   ),   data.frame(     Method            = "FlowSOM auto-k",     `k selection`     = "automatic",     `Best k in sweep` = cache$autok_point$k,     `Unimodality (%)` = round(cache$autok_point$unimodality, 1),     stringsAsFactors  = FALSE, check.names = FALSE   ),   data.frame(     Method            = "fastINFLECT",     `k selection`     = "automatic (inflection point)",     `Best k in sweep` = knee,     `Unimodality (%)` = round(inflect_at_knee$Unimodality, 1),     stringsAsFactors  = FALSE, check.names = FALSE   ) )  knitr::kable(tbl, align = c("l", "l", "r", "r"))

title: Sarle's bimodality coefficient — bimodality.coefficient
text: Computes Sarle's bimodality coefficient (BC) numeric sample, fast moment-based screen bimodality: $$BC = (g^2 + 1) / (k + 3 (n-1)^2 / ((n-2)(n-3)))$$ \(g\) sample skewness \(k\) sample excess kurtosis. BC lies (0, 1]; benchmark 5/9 (0.555) value uniform distribution, larger values indicate bimodal shape. BC offered lightweight, size-robust diagnostic complements dip test used fastINFLECT unimodality score inherited original INFLECT method. deliberately default QC statistic: driven skewness kurtosis can flag heavy-tailed strongly skewed genuinely unimodal markers (common cytometry) bimodal. Use rank markers/clusters follow-, confirm dip test.

title: fastINFLECT 1.0.0
text: Package renamed INFLECT fastINFLECT. exported INFLECT() function retained API continuity, documentation now explicitly frames repository fast reimplementation original INFLECT method.

title: fastINFLECT 1.0.0
text: Sub-tree memoisation. iteration.QC() now evaluates distinct SOM-node set . hclust/cutree metaclusterings nested, 2 * nNodes - 1 distinct clusters across whole sweep regardless densely set.samples k, cost longer grows number tested k values. Faster kernel. dip test now uses diptest::dip() statistic plus legacy-matched p-value interpolation, exact small-sample fallback, instead ~12x expensive dip.test() per cell. Compiled accelerators (Rcpp). inter-quartile-range spread test hot-path p-value interpolation implemented C++ (src/inflect.cpp), pure-R paths retained validated fallbacks package used without compiled code. Parallelism iteration.QC() now fans distinct sub-trees via fork-based parallel::mclapply() (Unix), replacing previous per-k foreach/doParallel loop. doParallel foreach longer dependencies.

title: fastINFLECT 1.0.0
text: inflection — original LL.4 log-logistic knee (unchanged default); kneedle — nonparametric knee (inflect_kneedle(), Satopää et al. 2011); threshold — smallest k reaching target unimodality (inflect_threshold_k(), controlled new target argument, default 0.95). directly encodes “admit cluster residual bimodal marker expression, without -clustering”.

title: fastINFLECT 1.0.0
text: New max.n.diptest argument (INFLECT() iteration.QC()) optionally caps number events used per (cluster, marker) dip test. removes sample-size sensitivity dip test — large clusters otherwise reject unimodality negligible deviations — making score size-robust. Subsampling seeded (seed) therefore deterministic. default NULL preserves legacy scoring path. New exported bimodality.coefficient() computes Sarle’s bimodality coefficient fast, size-robust diagnostic complements dip test (documented caveat: can -flag skewed--unimodal markers).

title: fastINFLECT 1.0.0
text: New vignette “Benchmarking fastINFLECT consensus metaclustering” times cost scanning k bundled Levine32 SOM: fastINFLECT’s memoised sweep versus original INFLECT loop FlowSOM consensus metaclustering, single ConsensusClusterPlus run per-k convenience pattern. also includes marker-expression histograms showing residual bimodality standard consensus partition versus overlapping fastINFLECT unimodal clusters. (Timings histogram data precomputed data-raw/make-benchmark-cache.R.) metaclustering comparison vignette now includes -cluster histograms Levine32 dataset, showing distribution per-metacluster marker-unimodality pass rates FlowSOM consensus, FlowSOM auto-k, hierarchical cuts, fastINFLECT recommendations.
